sourcedFrom: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed (UNDATED — no year is printed in the book)
cleanIntro: ⛔ THE BOLT BELONGS TO THIS RIFLE AND NO OTHER. ArmaLite serialise it: the last three digits of the rifle's serial number are inscribed on the bolt, and if you own more than one AR-50 you have to keep them straight. Beyond that the routine is short — bolt out on the bolt stop and that is all the strip a cleaning needs — and two prohibitions run through the whole book: no graphite lubricant anywhere near the aluminium, and nothing at all done to the trigger.

steps.title: Safety on, bolt back, and LOOK — it is a single-shot
steps.action: Finger out of the trigger guard, safety to SAFE, open and retract the bolt and look into the chamber. ArmaLite call this rifle very simple to unload and they are right — there is one place a round can be, so the chamber check is the whole procedure and there is no excuse for skipping it.
steps.quote:
While keeping your finger off the trigger and out of the trigger guard, merely 
move the safety to its “SAFE” position, open and retract the bolt assembly, and visually inspect 
the chamber to assure that it is empty.
steps.cite: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — CLEARING / UNLOADING THE FIREARM

steps.title: Bolt stop down, bolt out — and the cheekpiece may be in the way
steps.action: With the rifle unloaded and the safety engaged, depress the bolt stop and pull the bolt assembly to the rear and out of the receiver. If your cheekpiece is set low it will foul the bolt on the way out; raise or remove it rather than forcing the bolt past it.
steps.aside: NOTE: If you have the cheekpiece in a low position, you may need to raise or remove it.
steps.quote:
Depress the bolt stop (R-10) (See Figure 8) to remove the bolt 
assembly.  Pull the bolt 
assembly to the rear and out of the receiver.
steps.cite: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: ⛔ And that is all the strip a cleaning needs
steps.action: ArmaLite state it twice in the same box: further disassembly of the BOLT is a trained gunsmith's job, and no further disassembly of the RIFLE is needed for routine cleaning and maintenance. Taking the receiver out of the stock is possible and documented, but it is not part of cleaning — and it disturbs the bedding wedge and the two action screws that hold your zero.
steps.caution:
FURTHER DISASSEMBLY OF THE BOLT ASSEMBLY SHOULD 
ONLY BE CONDUCTED BY A TRAINED GUNSMITH.
steps.quote:
NO FURTHER DISASSEMBLY OF THE RIFLE IS NEEDED FOR 
ROUTINE CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE.
steps.cite: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — DISASSEMBLY

steps.title: ⛔ No graphite — it corrodes the aluminium receiver
steps.action: Whatever you clean and lubricate with, it must not contain graphite. ArmaLite give the reason: graphite encourages rapid corrosion of the aircraft-grade aluminium the rifle is built from. That rules out a good many dry lubricants that would otherwise look sensible on a heavy bolt gun.
steps.aside:
Graphite 
can encourage rapid corrosion to the aircraft-grade aluminum used in your rifle.
steps.quote: Under NO conditions should any lubricant containing graphite be used with your rifle.
steps.cite: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — CLEANING SOLVENTS AND LUBRICANTS

steps.title: Solvent then brush the bore — and never reverse a brush inside it
steps.action: Solvent on a patch down the bore first, then brush it out according to the solvent's own instructions. ⛔ Do not reverse the direction of the bore brush while it is still in the bore — a bristle brush dragged backwards against the rifling is how bristles come off and how lands get scored.
steps.aside:
Use cleaning solvent to clean the bore and chamber, the receiver, locking lugs and all areas of 
powder fouling, corrosion, dirt or dust.
steps.quote:
DON’T REVERSE THE DIRECTION OF THE BORE BRUSH 
WHILE IT’S IN THE BORE.
steps.cite: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — RECEIVER AND BARREL ASSEMBLY

steps.title: ⛔ Keep solvent OUT of the trigger — and if it gets in, lighter fluid
steps.action: Do not let solvent, lubricant or preservative drain down into the trigger mechanism; it will make it malfunction. ArmaLite give an unusual but explicit cure if it does happen — squirt lighter fluid into the mechanism to flush the contaminant out. ⛔ What you do NOT do is take the trigger apart or out of the receiver, and you do not adjust it: it is not user-adjustable and trying voids the warranty.
steps.caution:
DO NOT 
DISASSEMBLE THE TRIGGER MECHANISM OR REMOVE IT FROM THE 
RECEIVER.
steps.quote:
AVOID ALLOWING SOLVENTS, LUBRICANTS, OR 
PRESERVATIVES TO DRAIN INTO THE TRIGGER MECHANISM.
steps.cite: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — RECEIVER AND BARREL ASSEMBLY

steps.title: Chamber brush into the chamber AND the locking lugs
steps.action: Put a chamber brush on the rod, dip it in solvent and work it into the chamber and the locking lug recesses, pushing and twisting. The lug recesses are where fouling actually accumulates on a bolt gun, and a bore brush never reaches them.
steps.quote:
Install the chamber brush on the cleaning rod, dip it in cleaning solvent, and insert it into the 
chamber and locking lugs.  Clean by pushing and twisting the cleaning rod.
steps.cite: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — RECEIVER AND BARREL ASSEMBLY

steps.title: Bolt: lugs, bolt face, under the extractor lip, then the ejector
steps.action: Swab every outer surface of the bolt with solvent, take a bore brush dipped in solvent to the locking lugs, and clean the bolt face and UNDER the lip of the extractor. Then press the ejector in repeatedly to shake the accumulated brass shavings out of its hole, and lubricate it generously — ArmaLite's word.
steps.aside: Clean the bolt face and under the lip of the extractor.
steps.quote:
Press the ejector in repeatedly to remove accumulated brass shavings from the ejector hole 
and assure the ejector moves freely.
steps.cite: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — BOLT ASSEMBLY

steps.title: High-pressure grease on the bolt lugs, light oil everywhere else
steps.action: Lightly oil the firing pin and its recess and the outside of the bolt, then put a high-pressure lube or grease on the bolt LUGS specifically. Those lugs carry the entire thrust of a .50 BMG case and a light oil is not the right film for that job.
steps.quote: Lightly lubricate the bolt lugs with a high pressure lube/grease.
steps.cite: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — BOLT ASSEMBLY

steps.title: ⛔ No wire brush and no abrasive on the aluminium
steps.action: The forestock is aluminium. Wipe the dirt off the exterior with a clean cloth and nothing harsher — no wire brush and no abrasive of any kind. The anodising is the corrosion protection and it does not grow back.
steps.quote:
DO NOT USE A WIRE BRUSH OR ANY TYPE OF ABRASIVE 
MATERIAL TO CLEAN ALUMINUM SURFACES
steps.cite: ArmaLite Owner's Manual for ArmaLite AR-50A1 — AR-50A1 (the file ArmaLite publishes on its own product-manuals page); no edition code printed — FORESTOCK ASSEMBLY

deepAbsentReason: ArmaLite closes this one explicitly, in a boxed CAUTION on the disassembly page: "NO FURTHER DISASSEMBLY OF THE RIFLE IS NEEDED FOR ROUTINE CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE." The bolt is closed in the box directly above it — "FURTHER DISASSEMBLY OF THE BOLT ASSEMBLY SHOULD ONLY BE CONDUCTED BY A TRAINED GUNSMITH" — and the trigger is closed twice over: it is not user adjustable, and the manual forbids disassembling it or removing it from the receiver. ⚠ The book DOES document taking the receiver group out of the stock — bedding wedge screw, grip frame, two action screws — but it introduces that as something done "if for some reason, it is necessary", not as maintenance, and it disturbs the bedding that holds the rifle's zero. It is recorded here rather than presented as a deep clean. Nothing has been invented.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent on a patch, then a brass bore brush per the solvent's instructions
⛔ Never reverse the brush while it is inside the bore
Chamber brush pushed and twisted into the chamber AND the locking lugs
Bore, chamber and outer barrel lightly lubricated — do not over-lubricate

cleaning.name: BOLT
tasks: Locking lugs with a solvent-dipped bore brush
Bolt face and under the extractor lip
Ejector pressed in repeatedly to clear brass shavings, then lubricated generously
Firing pin and recess lightly oiled; LUGS get a high-pressure lube/grease
⛔ Bolts are serialised to the rifle — never interchange them

cleaning.name: ⛔ TRIGGER
tasks: Nothing. Not adjusted, not disassembled, not removed
Solvent kept out of it; if it gets in, lighter fluid is the maker's flush

cleaning.name: FORESTOCK (ALUMINIUM)
tasks: Clean cloth only — ⛔ no wire brush, no abrasive
⛔ No graphite-bearing lubricant anywhere on the rifle

reassembly: Bore confirmed clear of patches and brush bristles.
Bolt lugs greased with a high-pressure lube before the bolt goes back.
Bolt in and the bolt stop confirmed to hold it at the rear.
⛔ If the receiver was taken out of the stock: bedding wedge screw and both action screws back to tension, and the zero re-confirmed before the rifle is trusted.
Serial-number match on the bolt verified if more than one AR-50 is in the safe.
fncheck: Bolt back in and the rifle empty: work it and feel it run freely, and confirm the bolt stop holds it at the rear. Check the bore is clear of patches. ⛔ If you own more than one AR-50, check the last three digits of the serial number inscribed on the bolt match the rifle — ArmaLite serialise them because the bolts are NOT interchangeable.
